title: Zerubbabel
lead: Zerubbabel, a grandson of King Jehoiachin, led a group of exiles home from Babylon and, with the high priest Jeshua, rebuilt the altar and the temple in Jerusalem (Ezra 3–6; Haggai; Zechariah 4). He was governor of Judah under Persia, and Haggai called him the LORD's "signet ring." He appears in both genealogies of Jesus (Matthew 1:12–13; Luke 3:27).

sections.b: His name is Babylonian, Zer-Babili, "offspring of Babylon." Ezra, Nehemiah, Haggai and Matthew call him "son of Shealtiel"; 1 Chronicles 3:19 calls him son of Pedaiah, Shealtiel's brother. He returned under Cyrus or Darius I, laid the foundation of the second temple, and saw it finished in 516 BC (Ezra 6:15). Haggai and Zechariah hoped he would restore David's kingdom (Haggai 2:20–23; Zechariah 4:6–10), but he disappears from the record before the temple's dedication, and no king followed him. Sheshbazzar, "prince of Judah," who brought back the temple vessels (Ezra 1:8–11), may have been his uncle Shenazzar (1 Chronicles 3:18) or a separate official.
